transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

That stuttering is usually the vacuum's protection system kicking in because it can't get enough air. Since your battery is full, the most likely cause is a blockage or a wet/clogged filter restricting airflow. Please wash both filters (pre-motor and HEPA) in cold water only, shake out excess water, and leave them to dry fully for 24 hours before reassembling. If they are already clean and bone-dry, please check the hose and wand for blockages by looking through them or checking if a coin dropped in falls straight out.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal btw. washed the filter, water came out black lol, left it overnight on the radiator. pulses way less now but still a bit. no burning smell or heat or anything

The fact that it pulses less now suggests the black water was indeed restricting airflow, but the remaining stuttering means something is still blocking air or the filter isn't fully dry. Dyson filters take a full 24 hours to dry completely; placing them on a radiator can sometimes leave the core damp even if the surface feels dry. Please check the hose, wand and floorhead for blockages by looking through them or dropping a coin in to see if it falls straight out. Also, ensure the filter is completely bone-dry (not just cool) before testing again, as any residual moisture will trigger the protection pulse.
ok looked down the wand, big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom where the head goes on, pulled it out. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin

That's excellent news. To help prevent this from happening quickly again, try to empty the bin more often if you have pets, as fine dust can pack into the filter core even after washing. If the issue returns despite clear airways, let me know, but for now you're good to go.
